proposal.summary: Preserve the demonstrated cache reuse procedure. Decline search-stall and empty-output lessons because the visible snapshot does not establish those failures.

edits.title: Reuse fetched evidence across single and batched requests
edits.content: When single and batched fetching share candidate URLs, keep a URL-keyed cache of fetched text. Deduplicate candidate URLs while preserving order, exclude URLs already cached, fetch the remaining URLs together, and associate returned pages with their input URLs. Build extraction evidence from successful cached pages and reuse those same texts for source and verbatim-quote checks. Do not treat failed fetch responses as usable evidence. Reuse a cached rendering only when it covers the information needed for the current extraction.

additional_candidates.description: Deduplicate batched fetches against a URL-keyed cache and reuse cached evidence for extraction and citation validation.
Combine schema-validated extraction with exact coverage, source-domain, and quote-membership checks.

decisions.reason: The self-check reports empty output, but the visible trajectory ends during the block that calls refinement before assigning answer content and readiness. Extraction already produced five rows with no reported validation failures, and constraint calls completed. There is no completed final worker result establishing a submission failure or recovery; this snapshot is insufficient to justify a failure memory.

Both flagged batch queries returned four hits and recorded no new entities after the initial search had recorded all requested quantities. The task explicitly required batched search, and the batch supplied pages subsequently fetched for evidence. Neither occurrence establishes an unproductive search loop; empty discovery lists were appropriate for this fixed entity set.

The fetch block excluded the already cached URL from a deduplicated batch, retained four usable pages, and reused their text for extraction and quote checks. The worker reported no validation failures, and fetch records show four successful backend fetches. This supports a reusable cache procedure independently of the unresolved final submission. No existing entries require updating.

The nested schema and subsequent checks successfully validated the extracted rows, but the immutable base instructions already require schema-validated extraction, programmatic coverage checks, and verbatim evidence validation. Another entry would largely duplicate that coverage. The task-specific expected-value dictionary should not be preserved as an answer key.
